content: Dr. Robert Snow, a distinguished Professor of Malaria Epidemiology at the University of Oxford and a key member of the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Programme in Kenya, specializes in malaria research. Dr. Heiman Wertheim, a clinical microbiologist at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, Netherlands, focuses on antimicrobial resistance. The WHO guideline on mass drug administration of azithromycin to children under five years of age aims to promote child survival. This guideline was reviewed by 35 external peer reviewers, each with specific areas of expertise: Dr. Susan Abdel-Rahman from Rutgers University, USA, is an expert in pediatric clinical pharmacology. Dr. Johannes van den Anker from Children’s National Medical Center, Washington, DC, USA, also specializes in pediatric clinical pharmacology. Dr. Yin Bun Cheung from Duke-NUS Medical School, Singapore, focuses on biostatistics, particularly in human growth and development. Dr. Mathuram Santosham, a professor at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, USA, is an authority in pediatrics. Dr. Zulfiqar Bhutta, a professor at The Hospital for Sick Children, Canada, is also a specialist in pediatrics. Dr. Travis Porco from the University of San Francisco, California, USA, is a biostatistician with expertise in disease transmission. Dr. Robin Bailey, a professor at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, UK, specializes in tropical medicine. Dr. Daniel Chandramohan, also from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, UK, focuses on malaria and childhood pneumonia. Dr. Brian Greenwood, a professor at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, UK, is an expert in tropical medicine. Dr. Vijay Gopichandran from the Department of Community Medicine, ESI Medical College, India, specializes in epidemiology, general practice, bioethics, and public health. Dr. Antoine Andremont, a professor at the University Paris-Diderot Medical School, France, is an expert in microbiology. Dr. Peter Collignon, a professor at the Australian National University, specializes in microbiology. Dr. Naor Bar-Zeev from Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, USA, focuses on pediatric infectious diseases and statistical epidemiology. Dr. David Addiss from the Emory Center for Ethics, USA, is an expert in ethics. Dr. Karim Manji, a professor at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, Tanzania, specializes in pediatrics. Dr. Khumbo Kalua from the College of Medicine, University of Malawi, focuses on ophthalmology, particularly trachoma in Malawi. Dr. Kalua is also a co-author of the MORDOR study. The guideline development process was supported by a grant from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). The recommendations in this publication are based on the advice of independent experts who evaluated the best available evidence, conducted risk-benefit analyses, and considered other relevant factors. The publication may include recommendations for the use of medicinal products in ways not specified in their approved labeling, such as for unapproved indications, dosage forms, dose regimens, or populations. Stakeholders are advised to familiarize themselves with applicable national legal and ethical requirements. The WHO does not accept liability for the procurement, distribution, or administration of any product for any use.
